criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. A new test drives the drain entry point with a reader that returns unparseable output for the first item. It asserts that the reader's error text appears in the drain log line for that item and in the committed failed-reading record (a `git show` of the commit), that the reader ran exactly twice for the item (one re-read), and that the drain then ran the next item.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 110 passed, including `a_reader_that_gives_no_reading_is_read_once_more_then_skipped_with_its_error`. The test drives the real `drain::drain` through `real_steps_with`. Only the model output is faked: `turn.structured = None` for the first request's reader. It asserts four things. The reader ran 2 times. Two `drain` log lines for the item contain both '(not read)' and 'the reader returned no structured reading'. `git log --format=%B --grep 'the reader failed'` contains the error twice, under the subjects 'Read a request (the reader failed)' and 'Read a request again (the reader failed)'. The lander landed exactly the second item's job. The test reads the commit body with `git log` rather than `git show`; it is the same body text.

criteria.criterion: In that test the skipped item is reported with its reason, and the drain's stop reason is not 'repeated failure'. A second test (or a second part of the first) shows that when the re-read succeeds the item runs. Run with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria.evidence: The first test asserts all of these: `report.stop != Stop::RepeatedFailure` (it is TargetMet), `failed_item == None`, `jobs[0].outcome == "not read"` with the error in `reason`, a note containing 'skipped' and the error, and the error in `display::drain(&report)`. `a_re_read_that_succeeds_runs_the_item` passed: the reader ran twice, `landed == 1`, `jobs[1].outcome == "passed"` for the item, the lander has the item's job, and no note says 'skipped'.

criteria.criterion: A test in athena-core (run with `cargo test -p athena-core`) shows that a read whose reader output cannot be parsed commits a record or commit body that contains the `Proposal.reader_error` text.
criteria.evidence: Both passed. `a_reader_that_returns_no_reading_commits_its_error` asserts that `git show -s --format=%B <commit>` contains `proposal.reader_error`. The go re-read test asserts the same for the 'Read a request again (the reader failed)' commit. It also checks that the invocation seqs come out as [1,2,3] and that the job ends with one reading.

criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, the failed-reading commit is built using `reader_error`. `git diff` shows the error flowing into the commit body or record.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds `failed_reading_body(base, reading.is_none().then_some(error.as_deref()).flatten(), &redactor)`, where `error` is `read_for`'s third value, the one that becomes `Proposal.reader_error`. It is used in both `first_reading` and `correct`. The error is redacted, put on one line and cut to 1000 characters.

criteria.evidence: From Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1746 tests.

findings.summary: No test covers the `correct` path's use of `failed_reading_body`
findings.evidence: `correct` now builds its body with `failed_reading_body`. The planned demonstration said a correct variant was covered, but only `ask` and `go` are tested. The helper is shared, so the risk is low.

findings.summary: The drain line prints the reader error without redacting or truncating it
findings.evidence: `push` appends `one_line(reason)` to the console line, while the commit body redacts and cuts to 1000 characters. The same `reason` already reached the drain report before this change, so the only new exposure is the console line.

findings.summary: `athena go` on an unread job now reads it, where it used to print a hint pointing to `athena correct`
findings.evidence: run/mod.rs replaces the bail with `read_unread`. This is the change the reading intends and the changelog records it, but it also changes what `athena go` does when run by hand.

summary: The change does what the request asked. When the reader gives no usable reading, its error is written into the failed-reading commit body (redacted, on one line, cut to 1000 characters), and `athena drain` prints it on the item's line as `not read: <error>`. This fixes the cause, not just the message: before, `athena go` on a job with no reading only printed a hint, so two such results set the "repeated failure" stop and ended the run. Now `athena go` reads the job again, and the drain gives the item one re-read. If that also gives no reading, the item is skipped with its reason, the repeated-failure stop is not set, and the next item runs. I ran the drain tests (110 passed, including both new ones and the existing repeated-failure tests) and both new athena-core tests (both passed). fmt, clippy and the full test suite (1746 tests) passed in Athena's recorded checks. Only the six expected files changed. Three small findings, none blocking: no test covers the `correct` path's use of the new commit body, the drain line prints the error without redacting it, and `athena go` run by hand now reads an unread job instead of printing a hint.
